scope: Public-source scoping review of PQC market, engineering and research; not an exhaustive systematic review.

sources.title: Security & Risk Management Summit 2026 London: Day 2 Highlights
sources.review_locator: Stopping the Quantum Threat: PQC in Three Waves; key takeaways
sources.interest: Paid research and advisory publisher; public remarks only.

review.question: How might enterprise work be sequenced?
review.method: Public analyst conference summary.
review.finding: Key exchange, PKI/HSMs and signatures form distinct work waves.
review.boundary: Analyst timing opinions are not observed quantum capability.
review.implication: Map buyer tasks rather than a single algorithm purchase.

sources.title: Quantum Technology Monitor 2026: A commercial tipping point
sources.review_locator: About the report; Quantum technology market
sources.interest: Consulting research; underlying proprietary analysis not independently reproduced.

review.question: Is the wider quantum market a valid PQC proxy?
review.method: Public data, interviews and proprietary analysis are described.
review.finding: Computing, communication and sensing are covered together.
review.boundary: Broader technology revenue and economic value are not PQC TAM.
review.implication: Use as a category boundary, not a PQC forecast.

sources.title: Future encrypted: Why post-quantum cryptography tops the new cybersecurity agenda
sources.review_locator: PDF pp. 6,17,69; Research methodology and early-adopter definition
sources.interest: Consultancy research; self-reported organizational responses.

review.question: What does reported readiness actually measure?
review.method: Survey of 1,000 large organizations; April–May 2025.
review.finding: The activity group includes plans within five years.
review.boundary: Large-company selection and intentions do not establish deployment or revenue.
review.implication: Separate readiness, pilots, production and willingness to pay.

sources.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Market: Global Forecast to 2031
sources.review_locator: Overview; Report Code TC 9164; scope and methodology labels
sources.interest: Sells the forecast report; not audited realized revenue.

review.question: What market is the forecast counting?
review.method: Public commercial report summary; full model not inspected.
review.finding: The headline projects a defined solutions/services market.
review.boundary: Detailed definitions, reconciliation and estimation model remain inaccessible.
review.implication: Retain the estimate as publisher-specific, without pooling.

sources.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Market, 2026–2033
sources.review_locator: Market Summary; Report Scope; June 2026 edition
sources.interest: Commercial report publisher; full paid analysis not reviewed.

review.question: Why does this headline differ from peers?
review.method: Public report summary and segment definitions.
review.finding: A larger published base accompanies a different horizon.
review.boundary: The public material cannot reconcile its coverage with other estimates.
review.implication: Expose scope and methodology uncertainty before market sizing.

sources.title: Post-quantum Cryptography Market to Exceed $13 Billion by 2035
sources.interest: Sells research and market-intelligence products.

review.question: How should a long-horizon forecast be used?
review.method: Publisher press release for a commercial research suite.
review.finding: It reports expansion across a nine-year forecast horizon.
review.boundary: Public summary does not expose a reproducible category reconciliation.
review.implication: Keep its horizon and definition attached to every number.

sources.title: Quantum Cryptography Market: Regional Forecast, 2026–2034
sources.review_locator: Market definition; type segmentation; key market insights
sources.interest: Commercial market-report publisher; full report not inspected.

review.question: Is quantum cryptography the same market as PQC?
review.method: Public commercial summary segmented by QKD, QRNG and others.
review.finding: The named categories include physical quantum technologies.
review.boundary: This is an adjacent category, not an interchangeable PQC estimate.
review.implication: Exclude it from a purported PQC consensus.

sources.title: Postquantum Cryptography: Why You Need to Be Ready by 2030
sources.review_locator: Public title, publication date and Insights Abstract
sources.interest: Licensed analyst research; abstract-only access.

review.question: What does the accessible analyst record establish?
review.method: Public abstract of licensed research.
review.finding: It recommends a migration-program completion target.
review.boundary: The report body and detailed reasoning were not accessed.
review.implication: Log the recommendation without pretending to review the full report.

sources.title: Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Prime Factorization and Discrete Logarithms on a Quantum Computer
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: Which cryptographic problems are threatened?
review.method: Quantum algorithms for factoring and discrete logarithms.
review.finding: Polynomial asymptotic complexity changes the underlying threat model.
review.boundary: It does not supply a hardware arrival date or deployment cost.
review.implication: Separate mathematical possibility from an operational quantum attack.

sources.venue: SIAM Journal on Computing, 1997; arXiv v2, 1996

sources.title: Cybersecurity in an era with quantum computers: will we be ready?
sources.review_locator: Paper metadata; author ISACA article, Managing Quantum Risk
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: When must migration precede a hypothetical threat?
review.method: Paper metadata and the author's public timing discussion.
review.finding: Confidentiality lifetime and migration duration interact with the horizon.
review.boundary: The original PDF was inaccessible; this is a planning relation, not a forecast.
review.implication: Attribute the timing model's conceptual lineage to Mosca.

sources.venue: Cryptology ePrint Archive 2015/1075; related author article, ISACA 2015

sources.title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers in 8 hours using 20 million noisy qubits
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: What resources could an RSA attack require?
review.method: Fault-tolerant construction under explicit superconducting-platform assumptions.
review.finding: An estimate includes error correction and substantial physical resources.
review.boundary: Gate errors, cycle times and architecture are assumed, not available hardware.
review.implication: Treat the headline as a conditional engineering estimate.

sources.title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: Can resource engineering materially change estimates?
review.method: Arithmetic, storage and fault-tolerance optimizations under stated assumptions.
review.finding: The estimate changes qubit requirements and execution-time trade-offs.
review.boundary: It is not an experimental RSA-2048 break or a Q-Day date.
review.implication: Stress-test planning against changing resource estimates.

sources.title: CRYSTALS – Kyber: a CCA-secure module-lattice-based KEM
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: How is a practical lattice KEM constructed?
review.method: Module-LWE construction with a chosen-ciphertext-security transform.
review.finding: It connects assumptions, parameters and implementation trade-offs.
review.boundary: Historical Kyber is not byte-for-byte the final ML-KEM specification.
review.implication: Trace algorithm lineage while using current standards for implementation.

sources.title: CRYSTALS-Dilithium: A Lattice-Based Digital Signature Scheme
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: How can signature design simplify secure implementation?
review.method: Lattice signatures using uniform sampling and optimized arithmetic.
review.finding: Implementation simplicity is an explicit design objective.
review.boundary: Design intent does not certify every compiler or device implementation.
review.implication: Separate signatures, implementation assurance and current ML-DSA conformance.

sources.title: The SPHINCS+ Signature Framework
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: What alternative assumptions support signatures?
review.method: Primary abstract describes stateless hash-based signatures and FORS.
review.finding: The framework offers a different assumption and performance profile.
review.boundary: Full-PDF retrieval failed; proof details were not reviewed.
review.implication: Use it for lineage and diversification, not a universal ranking.

sources.title: Hybrid Key Encapsulation Mechanisms and Authenticated Key Exchange
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: When does combining schemes preserve intended security?
review.method: Formal KEM notions, combiners and authenticated exchange models.
review.finding: Hybrid guarantees require a specified construction and adversary model.
review.boundary: A proof for a construction does not validate arbitrary concatenation or deployment.
review.implication: Require combiner, authentication and protocol details.

sources.title: Benchmarking Post-Quantum Cryptography in TLS
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: How do network conditions change protocol costs?
review.method: Controlled Linux network emulation plus Internet experiments.
review.finding: Latency, packet loss and fragmentation change handshake behavior.
review.boundary: Historical candidates and platforms cannot supply current product benchmarks.
review.implication: Measure end-to-end conditions, not primitive cycles alone.

sources.title: pqm4: Testing and Benchmarking NIST PQC on ARM Cortex-M4
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: Which schemes fit a constrained microcontroller?
review.method: Board-specific functional, cycle, memory and code-size measurements.
review.finding: Resource limits exclude some implementations from the tested set.
review.boundary: The candidate inventory is a July 2019 snapshot.
review.implication: Keep hardware, implementation and measurement scope with results.

sources.title: pqm4: Benchmarking NIST Additional Post-Quantum Signature Schemes on Microcontrollers
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: How do additional signatures behave on embedded hardware?
review.method: Integrates candidates and records performance and exclusion reasons.
review.finding: Memory, portability and implementation availability affect feasibility.
review.boundary: A different board and candidate generation prevent naive historical comparisons.
review.implication: Preserve exclusions and configuration alongside performance.

sources.title: KyberSlash: Exploiting secret-dependent division timings in Kyber implementations
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: Can implementation behavior defeat an otherwise studied design?
review.method: Primary abstract and author notes report timing experiments.
review.finding: Secret-dependent division enabled key recovery in affected implementations.
review.boundary: The complete paper was not retrieved; this is not a break of all ML-KEM.
review.implication: Inspect implementation, platform and patch scope separately.

sources.title: An efficient key recovery attack on SIDH
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: Can a promising candidate fail under new analysis?
review.method: Primary abstract describes an attack exploiting SIDH auxiliary structure.
review.finding: The reported classical attack undermines the targeted construction.
review.boundary: Abstract-only review cannot audit the proof or generalize to all isogeny schemes.
review.implication: Keep cryptanalytic uncertainty and algorithm specificity visible.

sources.title: Frodo: Take off the ring! Practical, Quantum-Secure Key Exchange from LWE
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: What does reducing algebraic structure cost?
review.method: LWE construction with implementation and TLS experiments.
review.finding: Assumption choices create communication and computation trade-offs.
review.boundary: Its historical measurements are not current FrodoKEM or ML-KEM performance.
review.implication: Assess structural assumptions together with deployment constraints.

sources.title: Post-Quantum TLS Without Handshake Signatures
sources.interest: Research authors; no independent reproduction or proof audit performed here.

review.question: Can authentication be redesigned around KEMs?
review.method: Protocol construction, security analysis and implementation experiments.
review.finding: KEMTLS changes the handshake rather than swapping primitive labels.
review.boundary: Research-protocol results do not imply stock TLS interoperability.
review.implication: Distinguish protocol redesign from drop-in algorithm replacement.

sources.title: Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, NIST IR 8547
sources.review_locator: PDF pp. 8,20; transition approach and timelines
sources.interest: Government guidance, not vendor assurance or revenue evidence.

review.question: What changed in the finalized migration roadmap?
review.method: Final technical transition report.
review.finding: Risk priorities and cryptographic functions have differentiated transition treatment.
review.boundary: Federal-focused applicability is not a universal private-sector legal deadline.
review.implication: Map obligations and dependencies to the actual organization.

sources.title: Timelines for migration to post-quantum cryptography
sources.interest: Government guidance; implementation remains context dependent.

review.question: How does a staged migration programme look?
review.method: UK guidance separates discovery, priorities and completion.
review.finding: Planning and dependency discovery precede broad transition.
review.boundary: Indicative guidance is not a global statutory deadline.
review.implication: Use staged buyer tasks with jurisdiction stated.

sources.title: Project Leap phase 2: quantum-proofing payment systems
sources.review_locator: Project summary; report section 5 conclusion available in indexed extract
sources.interest: Official experiment summary; underlying results not reproduced here.

review.question: What does a payment-system experiment reveal?
review.method: Multi-party test replaces signatures in liquidity transfers.
review.finding: Compatibility changes and performance differences require coordinated preparation.
review.boundary: An experimental system is not evidence of sector-wide rollout.
review.implication: Budget for integration and negative-control testing, not algorithms alone.

sources.title: PQ.03 Guidelines for Telecom Use Cases V2.0
sources.interest: Industry-member guidance; full report body not reviewed.

review.question: Why do telecom use cases require separate migration plans?
review.method: Industry guidelines map architectures, standards and performance implications.
review.finding: Phased transformation depends on use case and stakeholders.
review.boundary: Public scope does not establish deployment rates or measured performance.
review.implication: Treat telecom as several buyer workflows.

sources.title: State of the post-quantum Internet in 2025
sources.review_locator: Opening traffic milestone and migration discussion
sources.interest: Provider self-report; no independent traffic audit.

review.question: What does a traffic adoption metric measure?
review.method: Provider reports its human-initiated traffic observation.
review.finding: The milestone concerns a defined traffic population.
review.boundary: It is not all Internet traffic or enterprise-wide readiness.
review.implication: Keep the denominator and covered cryptographic function explicit.

sources.title: iMessage with PQ3
sources.review_locator: Initial establishment, rekeying and hybrid design sections
sources.interest: Vendor engineering claims, not an independent product ranking.

review.question: What makes migration a protocol problem?
review.method: Vendor engineering account of hybrid establishment and rekeying.
review.finding: The design addresses ongoing conversation security as well as setup.
review.boundary: Vendor-defined levels are not a universal comparative standard.
review.implication: Evaluate the threat model and recovery properties.

sources.title: A new path for Kyber on the web
sources.interest: Provider-authored implementation notice.

review.question: Why does standardization require migration work?
review.method: Engineering notice describes Kyber-to-ML-KEM codepoint changes.
review.finding: The final specification is incompatible with the experimental variant.
review.boundary: The announcement is historical, not current browser support documentation.
review.implication: Pin versions and wire formats before interoperability claims.

sources.title: OpenSSL 3.5 Final Release
sources.interest: Maintainer announcement; not a recommendation to install the initial release.

review.question: How does distribution change the commercial layer?
review.method: Official library release announcement.
review.finding: Native support includes ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA.
review.boundary: Feature availability does not establish application configuration or assurance.
review.implication: Distinguish bundled primitives from paid integration and operations.

sources.title: Status Report on the Fourth Round, NIST IR 8545
sources.interest: Government selection account; complete technical report not reviewed.

review.question: How does the algorithm portfolio evolve?
review.method: Official fourth-round evaluation report summary.
review.finding: HQC was selected for further standard development.
review.boundary: A selection record is not itself a final algorithm standard.
review.implication: Keep selection, draft and final-standard status distinct.

sources.title: RFC 9954: Hybrid Key Exchange in TLS 1.3
sources.interest: Published technical specification; no product validation implied.

review.question: What does the published hybrid construction cover?
review.method: Informational RFC defines a hybrid key-exchange construction.
review.finding: Its scope separates ephemeral exchange from authentication.
review.boundary: Informational publication is not an Internet Standards Track status.
review.implication: Name the specification and its exact scope.

sources.title: A blueprint for formal verification of Apple corecrypto
sources.interest: Vendor-authored account; proofs not independently audited here.

review.question: Which assurance property is being demonstrated?
review.method: Vendor describes implementation proofs against algorithm specifications.
review.finding: Correctness, optimization and hardening are separate engineering criteria.
review.boundary: A correctness proof is not complete protocol or side-channel assurance.
review.implication: Ask what is proved, on which implementation and assumptions.

sources.title: Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard
sources.review_locator: FIPS 203: official abstract and final publication metadata
sources.interest: Normative source; algorithm function only in this review.

review.question: What cryptographic function is standardized?
review.method: Official normative publication abstract.
review.finding: ML-KEM establishes a shared secret.
review.boundary: The abstract does not establish implementation certification or current errata coverage.
review.implication: Use the standard's function, not a vendor-security shortcut.

sources.title: Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard
sources.review_locator: FIPS 204: official abstract and final publication metadata
sources.interest: Normative source; algorithm function only in this review.

review.question: What cryptographic function is standardized?
review.method: Official normative publication abstract.
review.finding: ML-DSA provides digital signatures.
review.boundary: The abstract does not establish implementation certification or current errata coverage.
review.implication: Use the standard's function, not a vendor-security shortcut.

sources.title: Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard
sources.review_locator: FIPS 205: official abstract and final publication metadata
sources.interest: Normative source; algorithm function only in this review.

review.question: What cryptographic function is standardized?
review.method: Official normative publication abstract.
review.finding: SLH-DSA provides hash-based signatures.
review.boundary: The abstract does not establish implementation certification or current errata coverage.
review.implication: Use the standard's function, not a vendor-security shortcut.
